Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 23:12:00 +0000
Subject: Lighthouse: Kestrel throughput/drop in p95 — need exec bridge

Team —

Kestrel is reporting a ~3x jump in p95 latency and a correlated spike in token error rates over the last 35 minutes for their production tenant (us-east, model: redwood-large-v1). Impact: their checkout flow is intermittently timing out for ~12% of requests. They surfaced this to their engineering lead and asked for an executive-level bridge.

What I know so far:
- Starts ~22:35 UTC, sustained from 22:50–23:05 with intermittent recovery windows.
- Error: 502s and incomplete streams, token-level decode failures.
- Throughput observed: drop from 1800 TPS to ~900 TPS on the shard serving Kestrel.

Immediate asks:
1) Vivek — can you confirm host-level saturation (GPU mem, host CPU, NVLINK errors)?
2) Marcus — please pull the model runtime logs and KV-cache hit rates; attach the last 30m traces.
3) Laura — customer comms: draft a short status note for Kestrel execs, include what we know and expected ETA for next update.
4) Rishi — if this is a capacity/stack issue we may need to spin warm nodes in that pool and consider falling back to redwood-large-v1-quant for a short window; advise risk.

I've put Kestrel's primary contacts in a watchful hold. If this looks like a platform regression we need an exec bridge in 15–20 minutes. I can host the bridge.

- Naomi

Subject: Re: Lighthouse: Kestrel throughput/drop in p95 — need exec bridge

Quick triage: host-level telemetry shows one of the serving nodes in the us-east shard reporting repeated PCIe link retries and process-level restarts on the runtime (3 restarts between 22:46–22:58). GPU memory and overall util are not OOM but the NVLINK errors correspond with elevated host IO wait.

Actions I'm kicking off now:
- Spawning two warm replacement nodes in the same pool; policy to rebalance traffic away from the affected host.
- Capturing core dumps and sending to infra team storage (service_logs_20261024.tar.gz).
- If new nodes catch up and KV-cache warm-up succeeds, we should see p95 drop within 6–8 minutes of cutover.

Risk: rolling traffic risks a brief increase in tail latency as caches re-warm; if we fall back to quantized variant as a temporary mitigation, quality regressions may appear on long-context requests.

I'll join the bridge in 10 to report progress.

—Vivek
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Daniel / Donna —

Thank you for the sample traces. Short status for your execs: we have identified transient host-level I/O errors affecting one of the nodes in your serving pool which caused the runtime to restart several times. Our team has rebalanced traffic off the affected host and is spinning two warm replacements now.

What to expect in the next updates:
- 00:08 UTC: traffic fully rebalanced to new nodes; we will monitor p95 and error rate.
- 00:12 UTC: second update with concrete p95 numbers and whether we need a short fallback to quantized model.

Immediate ask for you: please send any additional client-side traces for requests failing with 502s — they help correlate request IDs. We'll keep this channel dedicated to status updates; if you'd prefer a bridge, Naomi is hosting one now (invitation to follow).

Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 05:48:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Lighthouse: Kestrel throughput/drop in p95 — need exec bridge

Daniel / Donna —

Update (00:48 UTC): the replacements warmed and KV-cache hit rate recovered to 78% across the shard. Observed p95 improved from ~1.9s at peak to ~430ms over the last 18 minutes; error rates for token decode have declined to baseline (~0.4%). We kept quality on the primary model; did not roll to quantized fallback.

Root cause (preliminary): an intermittent PCIe/NVLINK hardware degradation on a single host produced repeated runtime restarts and IO wait spikes. Our infra team has isolated the host and scheduled a maintenance replacement; we will replace the physical host and run extended burn-in. Full RCA to follow once we have the hardware vendor report.

Customer-facing commitments we made:
- Provide 15-minute cadence updates until 08:00 UTC.
- Furnish the root cause summary and vendor report within 72 hours.
- Offer a one-month service credit to Kestrel if final RCA confirms vendor hardware failure leading to service degradation (commercial team will coordinate).

Attachments provided: redwood_kestrel_metrics_20261024.png, query_sample_20261024.sql, service_logs_20261024.tar.gz

If anything regresses we'll escalate to the incident commander and update Kestrel immediately.

- Naomi
